svg.title: A row, a table, and how Shensi's answers pick their rows
svg.desc: Top: one row, the 64 learned numbers the Comintern's network keeps for the zone question units:ccp:mountain_infantry, row 191 of its zone table after one update, drawn as 64 coloured cells, blue for negative and red for positive numbers up to ±0.15; its first numbers are 0.019, 0.002, −0.030, 0.021, −0.007, 0.018, −0.015 and −0.028. Left: the zone table, one row per zone question, 42,737 rows of 64 numbers; shown with their row numbers are rows 0 to 3 (possessor:ccp, possessor:dadao, possessor:japan, possessor:kmt), 14 (turn_start_possessor:ccp), 189 and 191 (units:ccp:militia and units:ccp:mountain_infantry), 307 (units:kmt:fighter, still all zeros because no kept sample had a KMT fighter), 9,844, 9,845, 9,992 and 9,994 (Comintern militia and mountain infantry counts and moves left), 29,446 (rail_to:land_china_hopeh) and the last, 42,736 (battle_order). The 9 rows Shensi's answers pick are highlighted. A fresh network's rows are all zeros; after one update 1,840 have moved. Right: Shensi's 9 answers, each 1, weigh ln 2 ≈ 0.69 each, so Shensi's vector starts as 0.69 times row 0 plus 0.69 times row 14 and so on to row 29,446; the sum's first numbers are −0.001, 0.137, −0.118 and −0.104. The network fetches only these 9 rows: Shensi's other 42,728 answers are 0.
